text:
Alex: quick sync — I'm rethinking where resilience responsibilities should live between the autoscaler and the pool operator. current layout blurs admission & machine lifecycle and it causes weird failure modes when the operator is transiently partitioned. thoughts?

Priya: agree, saw two outages last week when operator leader flip + slow node boot made admission hang. we need a clearer control surface. my take: operator owns node lifecycle (create/terminate, cordon/drain), autoscaler owns desired capacity signals and ephemeral headroom suggestions. admission should be a thin policy layer that can operate if either side is flaky.

TJ: +1. concrete failure we hit: autoscaler pushed desired=10, operator accepted but boot timed out -> admission thought nodes existed and allowed tokens leading to OOM on remaining nodes. we need a reconciliation TTL and a conservative admission when operator hasn't confirmed new nodes.

Elaine: proposal sketch: 1) split API: operator exposes explicit MachineSet status (ready_count, pending_count, last_update_ts). 2) autoscaler writes DesiredCapacity intent CR with generation id. 3) admission consults both: if operator's pending_count > 0 && last_update_ts < now - X then treat pending as unready and require extra headroom buffer. fallback mode: if operator unreachable, admission rejects requests with high-cost SLOs and accepts low-cost best-effort routes.

Alex: sounds good. on the generation id: should admission rely on autoscaler generation or operator-confirmed generation? i worry about races where autoscaler retries rapidly and admission flips flapping behavior.

Priya: admission ought to prefer operator-confirmed generation. autoscaler generation is advisory. admission logic: - if operator reports generation==g and ready_count >= desired_for_g -> allow normal admission. - if operator reports pending for g and operator.last_update_ts within window -> allow limited admission with prewarm tokens consumed. - else -> conservative deny/backpressure.

TJ: we need a small set of primitives, not a full protocol: fields: desired_for_gen, gen_id, ready_count, pending_count, last_update_ts, bootstrap_hint. make the bootstrap_hint optional for cold starts (operator can give an estimate). also add admission TTL per token so tokens can't live forever when op is partitioned.

Elaine: implementation detail: operator should expose an idempotent endpoint /status-for-intent that takes gen_id and returns stable snapshot. if operator is leader-elected, that endpoint is served by the active controller so reads are authoritative. orch-bot: will add a short story test for leader flip during scale up.

orch-bot: test ticket created: INF-4821 — leader-flip-scaleup-reconcile, assigned to TJ. :white_check_mark:

Alex: two more tradeoffs: 1) how aggressive should autoscaler be about prewarming vs cost? 2) where do we keep accounting for tenants' burst credits? my preference: autoscaler suggests ephemeral prewarm_count and a budget token that admission atomically consumes. operator doesn't manage per-tenant credits.

Priya: keep tenant accounting in the admission/controller layer. operator shouldn't need to know tenancy. otherwise operator gets complex and we risk coupling.

TJ: for the prewarm lifecycle: add a short-lived lease on prewarm nodes. operator can attach a lease annotation and automatically recycle nodes after TTL if no intent refresh. that prevents zombie prewarms.

Elaine: agreed. also: metrics we need immediately: operator.upsert_latency, agent_boot_time_p90, pending_count_gauge, gen_lag_seconds, admission_rejection_rate_by_cause. will add dashboards.

Alex: next steps: Elaine — add CRD sketch and endpoint shape. TJ — make test for leader flip + eviction. Priya — write admission logic pseudo-code and a small flow chart for failure modes. i'll draft a short RFC follow-up with the recommended primitives and a migration plan (rollout in three phases). aim to have PRs early next week. :rocket:
